### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-446107, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567, Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-9725554, Reactome:R-HSA-9927432)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic KRT14 variant (a hypothetical variant) —DISRUPTS→ KRT14 (HGNC:6416); KRT14 (HGNC:6416) —DISRUPTS→ Keratin intermediate filament assembly (GO:0007002); Keratin intermediate filament assembly (GO:0007002) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0007330); Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0007330) —LEADS_TO→ Skin blistering (HP:0000983); Keratin intermediate filament assembly (GO:0007002) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin pigmentation (HP:0001010); Keratin intermediate filament assembly (GO:0007002) —LEADS_TO→ Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis (HP:0000970). Pathogenic variants in KRT14 disrupt the assembly and integrity of keratin intermediate filaments, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including skin blistering (EBS) and features of Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn syndrome such as abnormal pigmentation and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in KRT14 associated with a loss-of-function mechanism for both diseases, or the absence of KRT14 mutations in affected individuals of either disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in KRT14 with a population frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD would challenge its causal role.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular pathway involving KRT14 and keratin intermediate filament assembly can inform therapeutic strategies targeting keratinopathies, potentially benefiting patients with both epidermolysis bullosa simplex and Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn syndrome.
